title: Relative Pronouns
summary: Connect ideas with que, quem, onde, and cujo in clear Portuguese sentences.

sections.heading: Que: the workhorse
sections.body: **Que** is the most common relative pronoun. It can mean who, that, or which, and refers to people or things.

examples.pt: A mulher que mora aqui é médica.
examples.en: The woman who lives here is a doctor.

examples.pt: O livro que você recomendou é ótimo.
examples.en: The book that you recommended is great.

examples.pt: Tenho um amigo que trabalha no banco.
examples.en: I have a friend who works at the bank.

sections.heading: Quem and onde
sections.body: Use **quem** for people, usually after a preposition. Use **onde** only for places; for non-places, use **em que** or **no qual/na qual** in formal writing.

examples.pt: A pessoa com quem falei foi muito gentil.
examples.en: The person I spoke with was very kind.

examples.pt: Esta é a cidade onde nasci.
examples.en: This is the city where I was born.

examples.pt: Esse é o assunto em que pensei.
examples.en: This is the subject I thought about.

sections.heading: Cujo/cuja
sections.body: **Cujo** means 'whose' and agrees with the thing possessed, not the owner. It is formal but important for reading and precise writing.

examples.pt: O escritor cujo livro ganhou o prêmio mora em São Paulo.
examples.en: The writer whose book won the prize lives in São Paulo.

examples.pt: A professora cuja aula perdi enviou o material.
examples.en: The teacher whose class I missed sent the material.

examples.pt: As empresas cujos funcionários participaram receberam certificado.
examples.en: The companies whose employees participated received certificates.

keyPoints: Que is the most common relative pronoun.
Quem usually appears after a preposition and refers to people.
Onde should refer to a physical or metaphorical place.
Cujo agrees with the possessed noun: cujo livro, cuja casa, cujos filhos.

commonMistakes.right: A pessoa com quem eu falei.
